content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:

Step 1. Create a profile on the official jobs portal (30 minutes)
Step 2. Attend the final ethics orientation (2 hours)
Step 3. Request official university transcripts (15 minutes)
Step 4. Sign the formal offer of employment (10 minutes)
Step 5. Complete the federal medical examination (3 hours)
Step 6. Pay the transcript processing fee (5 minutes)
Step 7. Upload a resume tailored to the job series (2 hours)
Step 8. Obtain a certified copy of your birth certificate (2 weeks)
Step 9. Research specific department missions (4 hours)
Step 10. Submit the initial online application (1 hour)
Step 11. Attend a government career fair (1 day)
Step 12. Draft a preliminary statement of interest (3 hours)
Step 13. Receive the final security clearance badge (1 week)

Step 21. Complete the SF-86 background investigation form (10 hours)
Step 22. Pass the initial HR screening call (30 minutes)

Step 29. Participate in the first-round panel interview (90 minutes)

Step 57. Receive a final start date (1 day)
Step 58. Submit a formal request for security adjudication (30 minutes)
Step 59. Review the workplace safety guidelines (1 hour)
Step 60. Finalize the entry-on-duty date (2 days)
Step 61. Complete the IT security training (3 hours)
Step 62. Register for the new employee orientation (30 minutes)
Step 63. Receive a temporary building pass (1 hour)
Step 64. Complete the lifestyle polygraph exam (6 hours)
Step 65. Provide a copy of Social Security card (5 minutes)
Step 66. Confirm availability for the start date (15 minutes)
Step 67. Wait for the background investigation report (3 months)
Step 68. Submit the completed application package (15 minutes)
Step 69. Attend a pre-employment medical briefing (2 hours)
Step 70. Submit a formal letter of intent (30 minutes)
Step 71. Provide proof of required vaccinations (1 day)
Step 72. Create a list of foreign contacts (4 hours)
Step 73. Verify the validity of the passport (10 minutes)
Step 74. Prepare for the panel interview questions (5 hours)
Step 75. Pass the final reference checks (1 week)
Step 76. Complete the initial health questionnaire (1 hour)
Step 77. Provide specialized skill certifications (20 minutes)
Step 78. Sign the conditional offer of employment (15 minutes)
Step 79. Request a DD-214 form (1 week)
Step 80. Document all previous foreign travel (5 hours)
